image_description: A Nile crocodile is partially submerged in murky water near a grassy bank. The head and upper back are visible, showing the characteristic armored scutes along the spine. The lower body and tail are obscured by tall green grass in the foreground and the water itself.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the head shows a tapered, V-shaped snout consistent with a crocodilian, distinct from the broader U-shape of an alligator.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and the jawline is at or below the water surface; individual teeth and their interlocking nature are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye bulge is visible, the resolution and distance prevent verification of vertical slit pupils or the presence of a nictitating membrane.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are clearly visible as two raised bumps at the very end of the snout, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal section confirms an elongated body covered in heavy, bony armor.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct longitudinal rows of large, keeled scutes are clearly visible running down the spine.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of dark grey/brown and lighter tan on the ridges, with a visibly rough texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral side (belly) is completely submerged and hidden from view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All limbs are either submerged or obscured by the foreground vegetation; digit count and webbing cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is largely obscured by the tall grass in the foreground, preventing assessment of its full length or compression.

alignment_reasoning: The image strongly aligns with the 'African crocodile' class. All testable checkpoints regarding the dorsal scutes, snout shape, and nostril position are passed. Several checkpoints were marked untestable due to occlusion (water/grass), but no contradictions were found in the visible anatomy. The texture and lighting appear natural.
artifact_reasoning: No AI-generation artifacts detected. The image exhibits natural photographic qualities, including realistic water reflections, consistent depth of field, and organic texture on the reptile's skin. Boundaries between the subject and environment are sharp and physically plausible.
